solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Biscuits served in small squares

parts.note: petit is the French word for small, familiar in English phrases
four is two squared, so fours are square numbers

explanation.surface: Someone describes how the biscuits come to the table, cut into little squares.
explanation.walkthrough: Four is the square of two, which is why 'squares' can stand for FOURS here.
explanation.definitionFit: Petits fours are small fancy biscuits or cakes served with coffee after a meal.

clue.text: Author Edgar maintains society attitude

indicators.note: to maintain is to hold or support, so the author's name holds the next letter

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe, the American writer

explanation.surface: A writer named Edgar is credited with upholding a particular social stance.
explanation.definitionFit: A pose is a stance or attitude struck for effect, physically or mentally.

clue.text: Rearranged stops near interchange

indicators.note: the letters of the two words that follow are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Bus or train stops close to a motorway interchange have been moved about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rearranged' looks like the definition but is the anagram signal; 'interchange' is a verb meaning to swap.
explanation.definitionFit: To interchange things is to swap their positions, which is a synonym for transpose.

clue.text: 13 exchanging money for king's word of approval

indicators.note: exchanging one thing for another means a letter of the subject word is swapped out

parts.note: the answer to 13 across, a subject
R, from Rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: The cross-reference reads as a puzzle instruction: swap money for a king's blessing.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation said when something is done to satisfaction, as in 'There! That's better', expresses approval.

clue.text: Note: Tense and time in dictionary left out

indicators.note: the note and two letters are placed inside the dictionary abbreviation

parts.note: OED is the Oxford English Dictionary
mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale
T is a grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A grammarian's memo: tense and time markings have been left out of a dictionary entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Something omitted has been left out or excluded; the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Flare up about American rejection

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the jumbled word goes round the abbreviation
up here means stirred or disordered, so the word is jumbled

explanation.surface: An American turning something down causes a flare-up of temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flare up' reads as one phrase, a burst of temper, but 'up' is the jumbling signal working on 'Flare' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A refusal is a no, a turning down of an offer or request, which is rejection.

clue.text: Leader leaves group of soldiers in square

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, which departs

parts.note: a squad is a small group of soldiers

explanation.surface: The commanding officer departs, leaving his unit standing on the parade square.
explanation.definitionFit: A quad, short for quadrangle, is a square courtyard, as in a college.

clue.text: Join in retinue making its way back

indicators.note: making its way back means these letters are read in reverse order
in says the letters sit within the word that follows

explanation.surface: Someone joins a royal retinue as it heads home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' takes ETINU from inside 'retinue' and 'making its way back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: To unite is to bring together, a synonym of join.

clue.text: Daughter and son accessing internet — mostly dodgy special services

indicators.note: accessing means entering, so the letter for son goes inside the jumbled letters
dodgy means unsound or suspect, so the letters are disordered
mostly means the word is used without its final letter

explanation.surface: A dodgy family online, with daughter and son signing up to shady special services.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last T of 'internet' to INTERNE; 'dodgy' rearranges it to INNERET; 'accessing' puts S inside to INNERSET.
explanation.definitionFit: A service is a matching set of crockery, so dinner sets are services of plates and dishes.

clue.text: Fellow with coat flapping on stomach's a general dogsbody

indicators.note: a coat flapping is thrown about, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: tum is an informal word for stomach

explanation.surface: A man with his coat flapping round his belly is the office drudge.
explanation.definitionFit: A factotum is an employee who does all kinds of jobs, literally a do-everything servant.

clue.text: Panic when spot is discovered on middle of cheek

parts.note: a spot or mark on the skin can be a scar

indicators.note: the central letter of the five-letter word is taken

explanation.surface: Someone panics on finding a blemish in the middle of their cheek.
explanation.definitionFit: A scare is a sudden fright or alarm, close to panic.

clue.text: At home carelessly fail to note increase

parts.note: in means at home, as in 'staying in'

indicators.note: done carelessly the letters fall into a disordered arrangement

explanation.surface: A homeowner carelessly ignores the rising cost of living.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflation is a rise in prices or a swelling in size, so an increase.

clue.text: Insulating material in Lyons is restricted by court orders

indicators.note: restricted by means held within, so the French word sits inside

parts.note: ASBOs are Anti-Social Behaviour Orders, issued by British courts
est is French for is, Lyons being a French city

explanation.surface: Building work in a French city is halted by court injunctions over a hazardous lagging.
explanation.walkthrough: An ASBO was a British court order restricting a person's antisocial behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Asbestos is a fibrous mineral formerly used widely for fireproof insulation.

clue.text: Subject of article covering European money

indicators.note: covering means the article goes first, on top of the remaining letters

parts.note: the definite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece reporting on the euro is the subject.
explanation.walkthrough: The article comes first, followed by M and E; the setter's order for the last two is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the topic or subject of a talk, essay or piece of music.

clue.text: Shows risky investment over ruined castle

indicators.note: in a down clue over means placed above the following part

parts.note: a spec is a speculation, a risky venture

indicators.note: a ruined building lies broken, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A speculator sinks money into a castle ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: Spectacles are impressive public displays or shows.

clue.text: Pass on reminder about letter

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the reminder goes round the spelt letter

parts.note: a prod is a nudge or reminder
cee is the spelt-out name of the third letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone passes on a reminder about a letter they were sent.
explanation.definitionFit: To proceed is to go forward or continue, a synonym of pass on.

clue.text: Cease hostility or risk extinction

parts.note: to end is to cease
anger is hostile feeling

explanation.surface: An appeal to stop fighting or face annihilation.
explanation.definitionFit: To endanger a species is to put it at risk, the phrase used of threatened extinction.

clue.text: New titles will embrace a touch of olde-worlde understatement

indicators.note: embracing means holding inside, so the jumbled letters surround the pick
new suggests a fresh arrangement of the word's letters
a touch of something is a tiny bit of it, here its opening letter

explanation.surface: Fresh book titles adopt a quaint old-fashioned understated style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges TITLES to LITTES, and 'will embrace' puts the O from 'a touch of olde-worlde' inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Litotes is a figure of speech using understatement, as in 'not bad' for good.

clue.text: Score's deuce, and there's a chance of a further score if this line is crossed

definitions.text: there's a chance of a further score if this line is crossed

parts.note: a score is twenty
a deuce is a two, in cards or dice

explanation.surface: A tennis-sounding score at deuce, then a hint of a rugby attack nearing the line.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby union the 22-metre line marks the attacking zone near the goal line, where tries become likely.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossing the opposition's 22-metre line in rugby puts a team within range of scoring points.

clue.text: Revolutionary doctor takes local father hostage in gorge

parts.note: Che Guevara, the Argentine-born revolutionary

indicators.note: takes, completed by hostage, means the doctor holds the next word inside
taking someone hostage means holding them captive, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: da is a dialect word for father

explanation.surface: A rebel medic seizes a villager's father and holds him in a ravine.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheddar Gorge is a limestone ravine in Somerset, England, also giving its name to the cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheddar is the best-known gorge in England, a famous deep limestone ravine.

clue.text: Tease pretty girl for becoming a plaything

parts.note: to rag is to tease
doll is old slang for a pretty girl

explanation.surface: Someone teases a pretty girl for becoming a mere toy.
explanation.definitionFit: A rag doll is a soft toy made of cloth, a child's plaything.

clue.text: Make note: Around noon arrive at National Trust

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the verb goes round the letter

parts.note: to come is to arrive
M stands for meridian, noon
NT is the National Trust, the British heritage charity

explanation.surface: Instructions to jot down that you got to a heritage property around midday.
explanation.definitionFit: To comment is to remark or make an observation, which is making a note.

clue.text: Shout about girl lowering head in a stupid way

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shout goes round the girl

parts.note: to cry is to shout

indicators.note: the head, or first letter, is moved down to the end of the word

parts.note: a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: Someone yells about a girl who has dropped her head in embarrassment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lowering head' sends the girl's first letter to the bottom of the word, as this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Crass means grossly stupid or insensitive, so crassly means in such a manner.

clue.text: Foreign film

definitions.meaning: the 1979 Ridley Scott science-fiction horror film

explanation.definitionFit: Alien means foreign or strange, and is also the title of a classic film.

clue.text: Suffer drastic ruin around second of October

indicators.note: around means the jumbled letters surround the pick
drastic suggests violent upheaval, so the letters are rearranged
the second letter of the month's name is taken

explanation.surface: Someone suffers drastic financial ruin in late autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drastic' rearranges RUIN to INUR, and 'around' puts it around C.
explanation.definitionFit: To incur a loss or penalty is to bring it on oneself and suffer it.

clue.text: Drawing of frigate briefly scribbled

indicators.note: scribbled suggests a messy scrawl, so the letters are jumbled
briefly means the word is shortened by its last letter

explanation.surface: A quick sketch of a warship, done as a scribble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' cuts FRIGATE to FRIGAT, and 'scribbled' rearranges OF plus FRIGAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A graffito is a single drawing or piece of writing scrawled on a wall.

clue.text: Imperfection in fine gold leads to loss and tears

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
AU is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: the leads of words are their opening letters

explanation.surface: A flaw in fine gold leaf leads to loss and tears.
explanation.definitionFit: A fault is a defect or flaw, a synonym for an imperfection.

clue.text: Judge's sitting with trouble in Parkhurst?

indicators.note: sitting with means placed alongside, so the pieces join

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for judge
to ail is to trouble

explanation.surface: A judge sits in court over a case of trouble at a prison.
explanation.walkthrough: Parkhurst is a prison on the Isle of Wight; the question mark shows it is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Parkhurst is one example of a prison, so the definition is by example.

clue.text: Playing such role with Ecstasy might be seen as lewd

indicators.note: playing about with the letters rearranges them

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: An actor playing a certain part while on drugs might look lewd.
explanation.definitionFit: Lecherous means given to lust, a close synonym of lewd.

clue.text: Some unlawful trafficking is extreme

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A claim that some illegal smuggling goes too far.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'is extreme' as the definition; 'is' is a link word, since the answer is an adjective and 'extreme' alone substitutes for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ultra as an adjective means going beyond the usual, as in extremist politics.

clue.text: Cut's said to be painful

indicators.note: said to be indicates a word that sounds the same when spoken

parts.note: to saw is to cut

explanation.surface: Someone's cut is reportedly hurting.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech the two words sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Sore means tender and aching, a synonym of painful.

clue.text: Act calmly in Hamlet. Personal magnetism's admirable

parts.note: Hamlet is a Shakespeare play
it is slang for sex appeal or personal magnetism
cool is slang for admirable or excellent

explanation.surface: A review: the actor in Hamlet has admirable charisma.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep composed and unruffled is the idiom's meaning, to act calmly under pressure.
